newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 7.29 bln reais in Treasury papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 7.29 bln reais in Treasury papers.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 7.29 billion reais in an auction of notes and letters, dealers said.

A total of 4.158 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury Letters known as LTNs. A total of 3.174 billon reais of 184-day LTNs, due January 1, 1998, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.238 percent a month.
The Central Bank also sold 984 million reais of 365-day, due July 1, 1998, at a call money rate of 2.358 percent a month.
A total of 1.626 billion reais was sold in two series of dollar-indexed National Treasury notes (NTN-D).

The bank sold 919 million reais of NTN-D notes, which are due on July 1, 1999 and pay an annual yeld of 10.795 percent. The bank also sold 707 million reais of NTN-D notes coming due July 1, 2000, paying an annual yield of 10.79 percent.

Some 1.506 billion reais were sold in National Treasury notes (NTN-H) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR). The notes, which are due January 1, 1998, pay annual yields of 12.65 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.
